source_evidence: Exact player 'Do they share the same pleasant demeanor as you? You seem exceptionally accepting of my return and interpretation of what is right.' asks Ysendre to contrast her peers and explain her own receptiveness. She describes Chancellor as intellectually courteous but transactional, Exarch as proud priest-ruler, and distinguishes their later affiliation from her actual former sworn service. These are her subjective impressions and informed firsthand relationships, not verified assurances of safety, cooperation, secret motives, their precise nature, sites or faction name. Caul candidly admits her acceptance reflects respect for Sovereign, accumulated evidence of V's identity, pragmatic value of peaceful recognition and an opportunity to earn continued stewardship rather than lose authority; she is not unconditionally obedient or convinced all V principles are correct, and wants voluntary trial to prove viable. She cautions peers may seek advantage from V's ancestry and recommends avoiding promises before understanding their interests. No new report to peers, magical influence, confession of undisclosed plots, fealty, unconditional reform, estate appointment, roll, combat, movement, rest, expenditure or other resource change. Day334~20:35. V next choice.
